:::{#exm-lebesgue-measure}
#### Lengths of some Borel sets

- $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \lebesgue([2, 5]) &= 5 - 2 \\
  &= 3.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- A single point has length zero:

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \lebesgue(\set{a}) &= \lebesgue([a, a]) \\
  &= a - a \\
  &= 0.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- The integers are the union of the pairwise disjoint single points
  $\set{0}, \set{1}, \set{-1}, \set{2}, \set{-2}, \ldots$
  (@exm-borel-sigma-algebra), so countable additivity gives

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \lebesgue(\mathbb{Z}) &= 0 + 0 + \cdots \\
  &= 0.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

- $\lebesgue([0, \infty)) = \infty$, because $[0, \infty)$ is unbounded.
- Lebesgue measure on $[0, 1]$ gives the whole interval $[0, 1]$
  the value

  $$
  \begin{aligned}
  \lebesgue([0, 1]) &= 1 - 0 \\
  &= 1.
  \end{aligned}
  $$

:::
